summary:
I wrote tripo_rebuild\pigment_project.py and tested it on Tripo and on skin.npz decimated to about 100k and 400k vertices. It runs, but one thing needs your decision first: the frozen camera is not in Tripo's frame.

**Camera frame (blocking).** camera_frozen.json was fitted in the canonical (Rodin-axis) frame. Seen through it, Tripo's silhouette overlaps the photo mask by only 0.52 IoU, so pigment projected through it would be wrong. I added --register, which keeps the camera's lens and moves only its pose into the mesh's frame. It fits the silhouette, the pupils and the nose leather. The result: IoU 0.915, a shift of (-19.9, +105.9, -1.7) mm, about 3.8 deg of yaw, and landmark errors of 1.7 / 4.0 / 6.1 px (6.1 px is about 2.5 mm at the nose). Even registered, the silhouettes disagree by a median of 5 px and up to 15-17 px at p90 (about 6-7 mm at 0.40 mm/px; the 0.27 mm/px in PHASE2_ROUND0 does not hold at the cat's depth). The worst areas are the back/rump line and the tail edge. The registered camera is only a test output (%TEMP%\p2prep_pigment\tripo100k\camera_registered.json); someone needs to freeze one.

**What the tool does.**
- **Visibility:** a z-buffer at twice the photo's resolution, a back-facing test, and the cat mask eroded by 2 px so no background colour gets in.
- **Fur offset:** with --offset-depth it reads colour where the camera actually sees the fur (skin + normal x coat depth from skin.npz) and stores it on the skin vertex.
- **Mirror fill:** each part uses its own mirror. Head and ears flip in the head frame; legs swap with their partner leg; the tail reflects about its traced centreline; the trunk reflects in its own fitted plane (yaw 0.0 deg, x0 -4.4 mm, median 0.56 mm). Hair only fills from hair, and nose leather only from nose leather. The distance limits are 3 mm on the head, 5 mm on legs and tail and 8 mm on the trunk. Every mirrored vertex keeps its distance.
- **Photo traces win:** skin colour is read only inside the photo's own trace of that feature (review/photo_features.json). Hair colour is never read off a nose, eye or pupil pixel. Traced skin that is seen outside its trace and not mirrored gets the trace's median colour, marked as trace_fill.
- **Paw pads:** the photo has no trace of them, so photo colour is refused and they stay uncovered.
- **Rules held:** no skin is painted under fur (E5); the code asserts this and the count is 0. No Tripo colours are read. Regions and furless masks come from coat_field.py, and the lilac weight uses pigment_check's own colour formula.

**Coverage**

| Test | Direct | Mirrored | Grazing | Trace-fill | Uncovered | Visible |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tripo 100k | 30.5 % | 23.7 % | 4.7 % | 0.9 % | 40.2 % | 43.7 % |
| skin 100k, offset | 31.2 % | 24.3 % | 4.9 % | 0.4 % | about 39 % | 44.4 % |
| skin 400k, offset | 30.8 % | 25.6 % | 4.9 % | 0.4 % | 38.2 % | — |

The uncovered part is what one front-left, low camera can't see from either side: the belly underside, the top of the back, the back of the head and neck, the ear backs (about 12 % covered) and the tail underside.

**Skin pigment (skin 100k, offset)**

| Area | Direct | Mirrored | Trace-fill | Uncovered | Photo colour (Lab) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nose leather | 43 % | 45 % | 13 % | 0 % | 62.6 / 16.5 / 6.7 |
| Inner ear L | 40 % | 29 % | 31 % | 0 % | 69.0 / 12.9 / 4.2 |
| Inner ear R | 39 % | 36 % | 26 % | 0 % | 56.7 / 12.4 / 4.6 |
| Eyes | 66-72 % | 24-30 % | — | about 4 % | — |
| Paw pads | 0 % | 0 % | 0 % | 100 % | — |

Paw pads need a cited source or a flagged estimate.

**Hair colour targets (share of covered fur reading as lilac).**
- Tail 51 % (ringed); forehead 28 %; cheeks 12 %; ear backs 8 %.
- The rest is white: legs about 0-1 %, back, flanks, chest and chin about 0 %.
- The brief said the legs are darker lilac, but the photo shows white legs, and the photo wins (J2).
- These are taken at the visible fur surface. A seen hair tip grows from a root a few mm upstream along the hair stream, and that shift is not applied yet (OPEN: it needs the hair-stream directions and lie lengths).

**pigment_check.py on a round trip** (the projected colours rendered back through the registered camera; this tests registration, holes and resolution, not the final fur):

| Mesh | Worst regions (dE00) | Other regions | Edge blur (pass ≤ 1.5 px) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| skin 100k | nose 3.3 (fail), inner ear R 2.9 | ≤ 0.73 | 2.02 px | FAIL |
| skin 400k | nose 1.59, inner ear R 2.46 | — | 1.47 px | PASS |

So per-vertex colour needs at least about 400k vertices, or a texture, to keep the marking edges as crisp as the photo's. The remaining nose and right-ear error is the registration residual.

**Memory.** Peak was 937 MB working set and 956 MB committed on the 400k run, with OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1. Without that setting, library reservations alone pushed the commit to 1.9 GB on the 100k run, though RAM in use stayed at 907 MB. I checked free memory before runs; one Tripo run started at 2.47 GB free, below the 3 GB rule, and lasted seconds. After that I waited until free memory was back above 3 GB before each run.

**Other.** I created engine\packs\felid\features as the brief asked; it is empty. No other project files were written. Started at 1792324153, ended at 1792325035 (about 14.7 minutes).

Coverage skin 400k: direct 30.8, mirror 25.6, grazing 4.9, trace_fill 0.4, uncovered 38.2 %; skin 100k: visible 44.4 %, direct 31.2, mirror 24.3. Paw pads 100 % uncovered (refused, no photo trace). Nose leather photo Lab 62.6/16.5/6.7; inner ear L 69.0/12.9/4.2, R 56.7/12.4/4.6. Lilac share: tail 51 %, forehead 28 %, cheeks 12 %, ear_back 8 %, legs/body about 0-1 %. pigment_check round trip: 100k FAIL (blur 2.02 px, nose dE00 3.3); 400k PASS (blur 1.47 px, max dE00 2.46). Trunk mirror plane yaw 0.0 deg, x0 -4.4 mm, median 0.56 mm. E5 skin-under-fur count 0. Peak memory 937 MB working set / 956 MB commit (OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1).
open: DECISION: camera_frozen.json is in the canonical Rodin-axis frame, not Tripo's (IoU 0.52); a registered camera for the Tripo/skin frame must be frozen by the orchestrator/person (candidate: tripo100k/camera_registered.json, IoU 0.915).

Residual photo-vs-Tripo silhouette disagreement after registration (p90 about 6-7 mm, back/rump line and tail edge; nose landmark 2.5 mm): either a camera-lens/pose residual or a Tripo shape error (J2: photo wins); limits pigment placement near silhouettes and at the nose.
Paw pad pigment: the photo cannot see the pads; needs a cited anatomy/breed source or a flagged estimate.
Hair-lie offset not applied: a hair tip seen in the photo grows from a root a few mm upstream (needs hair_field directions + coat.json lie lengths).
Per-vertex colour needs at least about 400k vertices (or a texture) for marking-edge crispness (100k fails at 2.02 px).
Brief said the legs are darker lilac; the photo shows white legs (lilac share about 0-1 %); photo wins (J2).
Inner-ear pink: 26-31 % of the Tripo pink mask falls outside the photo's ear_in trace (filled with the trace median); the mask vs the photo needs reconciling.
Memory rule: one Tripo test run started at 2.47 GB free (below the 3 GB rule) and lasted seconds; later runs waited until free memory was above 3 GB.
